plan: This is a second-price sealed-bid auction. In such auctions, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of the number of competitors, since your payment depends only on the second-highest bid, not your own bid (as long as you win). Bidding above or below your value only risks either winning at a loss or missing profitable wins. Therefore, the optimal strategy is straightforward: bid exactly my valuation of $27 to maximize expected profit.

In a second-price sealed-bid auction, the dominant strategy is to bid exactly my true value. This is because I pay the second-highest bid if I win, not my own bid, so bidding my true value maximizes my expected profit regardless of what others bid. Bidding higher risks overpaying if I win with a bid above value; bidding lower risks losing profitable auctions. With a value of $47, I will bid $47 to ensure optimal outcomes.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy: you win whenever your value exceeds the second-highest bid, and you pay that second-highest bid regardless of your own bid (as long as you're the highest). Bidding above value risks winning and overpaying above value; bidding below value risks losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, the optimal action is to bid exactly my private value of $12, ensuring maximum expected profit in this single-round auction.
